citations.F1: N+1 — one `actor` `fetchrow` per event, sequentially awaited, up to ~1,900 round trips per request — batch into one `SELECT ... WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: Dedup is O(n²) (`if ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` over a `list`) ... use a `set` for `seen`
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` uses synchronous `requests.get` inside an async handler, blocking the whole event loop ... replace with an async HTTP client
citations.F4: no index on `(org_id, created_at)` — add one (`CREATE INDEX events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`)
citations.F5: `_request_timings` list is appended to forever and never trimmed — cap it or replace with a rolling/reservoir metric
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict that never evicts — bound it (LRU with max size, or TTL)
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal as-is ... 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = up to 4,800 Postgres connections, likely past `max_connections`); revisit caching only after the fixes below
